topic_tag: a monastery above a mountain road
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In those books, one historian argues, it appears as the valley's ______.

worlds.passage: From 1400 to 1700 a monastery stood above the only road through a mountain valley, and its account books survive. Its wine was poured at the gate, and in most years what drovers and merchants paid there exceeded the rent from its fields. Townspeople came up for weeks each September, paid by the day to pick grapes. Its three hundred books were bought at city fairs, bills of sale still pinned inside. Its iron-bound cellar chests filled with coin each autumn and were emptied by spring into the building of a new chapel. In those books, one historian argues, it appears as the valley's ______.
worlds.explanation: Wine was poured at the gate, and in most years what drovers and merchants on the road paid came to more than the rent from its fields, so the monastery made its living serving drink to travelers: it was the valley's "tavern." A "sanatorium" takes in the sick to recover, but the townspeople who came for weeks each September were paid by the day to pick grapes. A "scriptorium" is where books are written out, but its three hundred books were bought at the city fairs. A "vault" keeps valuables safe, but its chests were emptied each spring to pay for a new chapel.

sanatorium.inference: guests who are paid by the day for picking grapes are hired workers at harvest, not patients, so the weeks they spent there were labor, not recovery

worlds.passage: From 1400 to 1700 a monastery stood above the only road through a mountain valley, and its account books survive. Townspeople came up each autumn with letters from doctors in the city and stayed through the winter in rooms facing the sun, and the books list milk, eggs and firewood bought for that wing. Drovers stopping at its gate got bread and one night's bed, entered in the books as alms. Its iron-bound cellar chests held that wing's bedding through the summer. Its few books were printed in the city and bought there. In those books, one historian argues, it appears as the valley's ______.

A "tavern" sells food and drink to travelers, but the drovers who stopped at its gate got bread and a bed recorded as alms, a gift. A "vault" keeps valuables safe, but its iron-bound chests held the guest wing's bedding. A "scriptorium" is where books are written out, but its few books were printed in the city and bought there.

worlds.passage: From 1400 to 1700 a monastery stood above the only road through a mountain valley, and its account books survive. Drovers stopping at its gate got bread and one night's bed, entered in the books as alms. Townspeople came up for weeks each September, paid by the day to pick grapes. worlds.passage: From 1400 to 1700 a monastery stood above the only road through a mountain valley, and its account books survive. Every farm deed lay behind two iron doors in its cellar, written by the duke's clerks in town and carried up; at each sale, buyer and seller climbed up to see the name changed. The duke paid yearly to keep his own chests there. Drovers stopping at its gate got bread and one night's bed, entered in the books as alms.
